messages.author: f3d71ca39a57d9c3
messages.subject: Interpreting simulation study model validation
parts:
Hi folks,

I ran a simulation study to test the performance of a model according to Zuur et al., 2017 (Beginner's Guide to Spatial, Temporal and Spatial-Temporal Ecological Data Analysis with R-INLA). That involved generating 1000 simulated data sets from the model and comparing the number of zeros in the observed data set vs the number of zeros in the simulated data set. 

The result of the study showed that the simulated data had a larger number of zeros compared to the observed data. What are the possible reasons that could contribute to this? missing covariates? zero inflation? I know each case is specific, but i would like to know of the potential reasons as part of a discussion of the results of the model.

Thanks in advance,
Sophie

messages.author: f3d71ca39a57d9c3
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Interpreting simulation study model validation
parts:
The data are fisheries-independent survey records that were very zero-inflated, so i thinned them a little. The study area is quite large (most of the NE Atlantic shelf area).

I tried the following formulations:
GLM (one variable only) - Overestimates no of zeros
GAM - Simulated data underestimate the number of zeros compared to observed (left skewed histogram)
GAMM - Simulated data estimate a similar number of zeros to observed (right skewed but still high numbers of simulated datasets overestimating)
Temporal GAMM  - Similar to GAMM, frequency plot of simulated data sets is a little more centred around the no of zeros in observed data
Temporal GAMM + SPDE - Overestimates

So i suppose it must be the SPDE term causing an issue then.... but the SPDE term does improve model according to DIC... What do you think?

Thanks again, i appreciate that so many things could be causing this problem.
Sophie

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Interpreting simulation study model validation
parts:
Its hard to tell what is going on, With the SPDE you have to be carefull
with the priors, usually the pc-priors for them works well.

There is also this new families,

inla.doc("0poisson")

which includes the neg.binomial, for which allow you to mode the zero-
probabilty (ie non-constant).

If the number of zero's is your aim, you do not need to consider the
DIC. You can also consider models that separate the 0's, so there is no
overlap, maybe it gets easier then.

Best
Havard
